instances.text: Begin with an empty book. Limits: A sell 2 at 105; B sell 32 at 109; C buy 8 at 104. Cancel A, then market buy 40. How many shares actually fill?
instances.spoken_text: Begin with an empty book. Limits: A sell two at one hundred and five; B sell thirty-two at one hundred and nine; C buy eight at one hundred and four. Cancel A, then market buy forty. How many shares actually fill?

follow_up.question: Why does bid quantity not help fill a market buy?
follow_up.reference: The market buy needs sellers. Existing bids are other buyers and cannot supply the required opposing shares.
